- References: none blocked. Render gate never refused.. Judge: A is better in all four pairs, by a wide margin each time. The B frames show real scale: dense skylines, recognisable waterfront landmarks, a warm haze, umbrella-carrying crowds and a boat wake. But they fall short of premium quality in the same five ways every time. First, materials and facades are weak: window grids repeat, pale towers, a wall and domes have no texture, and landmark structures are plain white shapes. Second, there is little life at ground level: paving is empty, walls are blank, and the city has no traffic and only one boat. Third, the foregrounds carry too little information and take up a large share of the frame (pair 1's concrete slab, pair 2's empty right half). Fourth, the lighting is even and washed out, with no strong key light, bloom or contrast to give a cinematic feel. Fifth, the hero subject in pair 3 is under-rendered: a dark helicopter with a hard-edged rotor disc. Pair 4, the elevated vista, is closest, because B's skyline density can compete there. Even so, the crude tiled tower in its near field and the blank slabs give it away. In order of priority, the fixes are: a facade and material pass that removes every untextured slab and flat repeating window tile, then a near and midground fill with props, planting and at least 10 pedestrians in each street-level shot, then active shopfronts at street level and traffic on roads, bridges and water, and finally a stronger directional key light with bloom and aerial perspective.
